title: Special Topics in Japanese Aesthetic Practices

sections.note: Topic: Ikebana (Japanese Flower Arrangement), Through lectures, selected readings, and hands-on experience of Ikebana (the art of Japanese flower arrangement), students will gain new perspectives and appreciation for the beauty of nature while exploring the artistic techniques and traditions of Japanese floral arts. Instructor approval required. Students must apply at https://go.illinois.edu/ikebana

The main theme of this course is the exploration of how the Japanese Tea Ceremony can be applied to everyday life. Through the study of the Tea Ceremony and the Zen worldview, it is hoped that students will acquire a better understanding of Japanese culture and also come to see their own culture in a new light. This section is for Chancellor's Scholars.

Topic: Zen Heart, Tea Mind. This course examines the meaning, history, and people connected to popular phrases found in Zen Buddhism and in the world of Japanese tea ceremony. This course is comprised of online lectures/discussions and two in-person activity days on 1/21 and 3/11. Students are required to register for the online lecture and in-person section. 2 seats are reserved for ARTJ minors. On 12/1 any remaining seats will become available to all majors.
